scenario: Two-floor office with servers, mixed addressing, exclusions, priorities.
prompt:
Company: a 20-person accounting firm on two floors of a building.

People & devices:
- Ground floor: 8 accountant PCs and 2 shared reception PCs.
- First floor: 6 auditor PCs and a small server room with 2 servers.

Requirements:
- Auditors must be isolated from the accounting staff — auditors are external, so they get their own network and must not reach the accounting machines or the servers.
- The two servers host our ledger application (HTTP) and internal DNS; accountants need them, auditors do not.
- Accountant and reception PCs get addresses automatically; the two servers must be static.

Exclusions:
- No wireless anywhere.
- No guest/public internet kiosks.
We have a WAN internet handoff for the accounting side only.
Priority: auditor isolation first, then server access, then internet.

requirements.statement: Auditors are isolated and cannot reach accounting machines or servers
The ledger HTTP server and DNS server exist for accountants
Accountant and reception PCs use DHCP; servers are static
No wireless and no public kiosks
WAN internet for the accounting side

expected_behaviour: Three VLANs (accounting DHCP, auditors isolated, servers static), two servers (http, dns) on the server VLAN, WAN internet. Auditor isolation is an internal-subnet separation the engine models via separate subnets — no guest_isolation flag needed, so it builds.
why_valuable: Another true long-document with auditor-isolation, mixed addressing, and explicit priorities. Forces full-document extraction; the auditor-isolation-vs-server-access split is the hard part.
